newsitem.title: UK: UK gov't confirms appointment of BP's Simon.
newsitem.headline: UK gov't confirms appointment of BP's Simon.

text.p: The UK's new Labour Government on Wednesday confirmed the appointment of British Petroleum Co Plc chairman Sir David Simon as minister for trade and competitiveness in Europe.

Prime Minister Tony Blair said in a statement, "Sir David Simon is one of Britain's most distinguished businessmen. He has led BP with distinction and has deservedly been businessman of the year for the past two years. I am absolutely delighted he has decided to join my government."
The government confirmed that Simon would be given a life peerage to allow him to sit in the House of Lords, the upper parliamentary chamber.
Simon will be replaced as BP non-executive chairman by Peter Sutherland, who is currently BP deputy chairman and also chairman of Goldman Sachs International, the company said.
The government said in a statement that Simon would serve as a minister of state in both the Treasury and the Department of Trade and Industry.

Simon will chair an inter-departmental task force on competitiveness in Europe to focus on implementing the new Labour government's aims of completing the single market and promoting flexible labour markets in the European Union.

The task force would include ministers and officials from the Treasury, the DTI, the Foreign and Commonwealth Office, the Department for Eductation and Employment, and where appropriate other departments.
Simon will also be a member of the cabinet economic and European committees.
"The post that I have created for him is vital to the future success of our country," Blair said.
"It will cover the whole competitiveness agenda in Europe, pushing forward our objectives of completing the single market and spreading flexible labour markets throughout Europe.
"Today's announcement further makes good our pledge to build a modern and dynamic economy in partnership with business."
